jobs.description:
About Contra Labs

Contra Labs sits at the intersection of human creativity and AI. We partner with leading AI labs and product companies to improve their tools across design, video, development, and beyond. Our research is grounded in how top creatives actually work, studying the patterns behind what gets created, what gets chosen, and what resonates. We believe human input will always be at the center of net new creation, and our mission is to help shape technology so human creativity can be amplified to create what today is unimaginable.

By joining the Contra Labs network you gain access to paid projects with some of the most innovative companies building the next generation of creative and AI-powered tools.

How It Works

This is an application to join the network and be eligible for roles as they arise. Projects are staffed on an as-needed basis, typically 5 to 10 hours at a time, though some may extend into longer engagements. In unique cases, we may have full-time roles available as well. When a project matches your skill set, we'll reach out with details and timeline.

To Join the Network

Portfolio review - We'll assess your Contra profile and portfolio for strength in content design, with a focus on ad creative and performance-driven visual content.
Record a 30 second intro video - Share a quick 30 second introduction so we can get to know you.
Complete profile - Once you’ve applied, we recommend completing your profile for better job matches and setting up your wallet so you can get paid when a job comes through.

Evaluate AI-generated 3D scenes, interactive environments, simulations, and spatial experiences for visual and technical quality
Provide clear, structured feedback on scene composition, lighting, materials, physical dynamics, asset integration, interaction, and overall visual coherence
Help define quality benchmarks and evaluation criteria for what great AI-generated 3D experiences should look and feel like
Identify common failure modes in AI-generated 3D work, from broken physics and interactions to poor spatial composition or inconsistent visual feedback
Create reference examples, prototypes, or "golden" outputs that demonstrate best-in-class 3D execution
Contribute to research exploring how AI models can better understand and generate interactive 3D experiences

What We're Looking For

Strong portfolio showcasing high-quality 3D design, interactive environments, or spatial experiences
Strong understanding of 3D composition, lighting, materials, animation, and visual coherence
Ability to articulate creative and technical feedback clearly and constructively
Strong 3D design instincts and awareness of contemporary visual culture, 3D trends, and emerging digital aesthetics
Comfort working in fast-paced, experimental environments (experience with AI, 3D tools, or creative technology is a plus)

Thorough knowledge of EPD equipment design, construction and operation.
Working knowledge of reliability systems, root cause failure analysis, predictive maintenance techniques and computerized maintenance management systems such as SAP-PM is preferred.
Demonstrated leadership and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively with team members at all levels of the organization.
Excellent written, verbal, consulting and technical-training skills, including the ability to teach in classroom and field settings.

jobs.title: Flatiron Research Fellow - Biological Transport Networks, Center for Computational Biology
jobs.description:
Description
The Center for Computational Biology (CCB), an in-house research center of the Simons Foundation ’s Flatiron Institute , is actively seeking enthusiastic, full-time post-doctoral Flatiron Research Fellows to join its Biological Transport & Networks Group .   The start date is flexible, with the Fellow expected to begin no later than September 2027. Applications will be reviewed beginning in Fall 2026 and considered on a rolling basis until the positions are filled.

ABOUT THE CENTER FOR COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY 

CCB has a twofold mission: to develop the rigorous modeling tools and theory needed for understanding biological processes, and to create computational frameworks that will facilitate the analysis of the large, complex data sets being generated by quantitative experimental technologies. To accomplish this, CCB brings together experts in various biological domains (including genomics, molecular, cellular, and developmental biology) whose approaches are informed by the modern computational tools of applied mathematics, statistical inference, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), biophysics, and computer science. The goal: to enable CCB to undertake ambitious, long-term research projects that transcend conventional disciplinary boundaries and that lead to a quantitative and predictive understanding of biological phenomena; and to develop high-quality, well-tested, versatile and extensible software across its research areas.  

CCB currently comprises more than 50 scientists at career stages from Ph.Ds through senior scientists, as well as visiting scientists and guest researchers, affiliated graduate students and interns. Together, the CCB scientific staff are pioneering an approach to biology in which theory,computation, and experimentation are integrated, from problem conceptualization onwards. This approach enables CCB to tackle not only recognized, fundamental problems in biology that have so far eluded solution, but also, because of the value placed on curiosity-driven research, to find and develop new areas of biological inquiry.

ABOUT THE BIOLOGICAL TRANSPORT & NETWORKS GROUP

Led by Eleni Katifori, the Biological Transport Networks group uses theory and computation, in close collaboration with experimentalists, to understand how biological networks develop, remodel, and function. We investigate how local physical processes—including fluid flow, tissue deformation, and transport of nutrients and signaling molecules—give rise to network architecture and collective behavior. Our work connects physics, applied mathematics, and biology, seeking general principles that explain both the diversity of transport networks across organisms and the common constraints that shape their organization.

Current research spans vertebrate vascular development and remodeling, circulation driven by cilia and body contractions in jellyfish, the interplay between tissue mechanics and vascular transport, and transport-informed models of neuronal growth and maturation. Central questions include how adaptation produces hierarchical or looped architectures, how pulsatile flows influence network development and function, and how nonlinearities and vessel compliance affect transport. We combine analytical models, large-scale numerical simulations, artificial intelligence and machine learning methods, and quantitative analysis of experimental data to connect processes at the scale of individual vessels with the behavior of entire networks. Alongside these biological questions, we investigate how adaptive physical networks can learn, store memory, and perform tasks through local interactions, with applications to fluidic and mechanical systems.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

Flatiron Research Fellows in CCB are individuals at the postdoctoral level with backgrounds in one or more of the following areas: applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines.

Reporting to the Group Lead, Fellows are expected to carry out an active research program that can be independently directed and/or involve substantial collaboration with other members of CCB or the Flatiron Institute. In addition to their research, Fellows help build the rich scientific community at CCB and the Flatiron Institute by participating in seminars, colloquia, and group meetings; developing their software, mathematical and computational expertise through internal education opportunities; and sharing their knowledge through scientific publications, presentations, and/or software releases, with the financial support of the Institute. Fellows have access to the Flatiron Institute’s powerful scientific computing resources.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Performing theoretical and computational research

Developing, implementing and maintaining scientific software

Participating in the organization of CCB and Flatiron-wide collaborative activities including seminars, workshops and meetings

Participating in the preparation of manuscripts for publication and of presentations at scientific conferences

Assisting in student mentorship

Sharing expertise and providing training and guidance to CCB staff and visitors as needed.

Fellows will be based, and have a principal office or workspace, at the Simons Foundation’s offices in New York City.  The initial appointments for Flatiron Research Fellows are generally for two years, with the possibility of renewal for a third year, contingent on performance. FRFs may be eligible for subsidized housing within walking distance of CCB. 
Qualifications
Education

Ph.D. in a relevant field (applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines)

Related Skills & Other Requirements

Demonstrated abilities in mathematical modeling, analysis and/or scientific computation, scientific software and algorithm development, data analysis and inference, and image analysis

Ability to do original and outstanding research in computational biology, and expertise in computational methods, data analysis, software and algorithm development, modeling machine learning, and scientific simulation 

Ability to work well in an interdisciplinary environment, and to collaborate with experimentalists

Strong oral and written communication, data documentation, and presentation skills

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The full-time annual compensation for this position is USD $95,000. In addition to competitive salaries, the Simons Foundation provides employees with an outstanding benefits package.
Application Instructions
To apply, please submit the following via the application portal:

Cover Letter, which should include a summary of applicants’ most significant contributions in graduate school

Curriculum vitae with publications list and, if relevant, links to software 

Research statement of no more than three (3) pages describing the applicant’s past important results, current and future research interests which may include both scientific topics and algorithm and software development, and potential synergies with activities at CCB

Two (2) letters of recommendation 

Applications will generally be reviewed beginning November 2026, and will be considered on a rolling basis until the positions are filled. For full consideration, candidates are strongly encouraged to submit their complete application by November 30, 2026. 

SELECTION CRITERIA

Applications will be evaluated based on: 

past research accomplishments

the proposed research program

the synergy of applicant’s expertise and research proposal topic with existing CCB staff and research programs, and potential to cross boundaries between CCB groups and/or the Flatiron Institute’s other research centers.

Any queries about the application process or about CCB should be directed to ccbjobs@flatironinstitute.org. Queries about CCB may also be directed to scientific staff at CCB. 

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Application Materials

The Flatiron Institute values authenticity, originality, and transparency throughout the application and hiring process. Applicants are expected to submit application materials that reflect their own original work, experiences, ideas, writing, and scientific or professional judgment. The use of AI-based tools may be appropriate for limited purposes during the hiring process, such as editing, formatting, or code review. However, application materials, including research statements, cover letters, personal statements, and other writing samples, should not be substantially authored or generated by AI systems.

Applicants are encouraged to disclose any significant or material use of AI tools in the preparation of their application materials or throughout the hiring process. The Flatiron Institute does not use AI-based tools to screen applicants.

Many of the greatest ideas and discoveries come from a diverse mix of minds, backgrounds, and experiences. The Simons Foundation is committed to advancing basic science and mathematics to benefit humankind and expand our collective understanding of our world. jobs.description:
Description

Drive transformation for leading Healthcare & Life Sciences organizations while shaping the future of patient care, drug discovery, and clinical innovation through AWS cloud and AI solutions.

Partner with senior leaders at global HCLS enterprises to accelerate their cloud adoption journey, delivering measurable business outcomes and strategic value.

About The Role

Customer Solutions Managers (CSMs) at AWS are obsessed with accelerating customer cloud adoption and driving measurable value from cloud investments. As a CSM in Healthcare & Life Sciences, you'll partner with senior leaders and engineering teams at global organizations to strategize and manage their end-to-end cloud and AI transformation journeys.

We help Healthcare & Life Sciences organizations adopt advanced cloud and AI solutions while migrating existing workloads to the cloud. Together with customers, we shape and execute strategies to build mindshare and broaden the use of AWS offerings across their enterprises.

If you are excited about the prospect of using your cloud architecture experience to assist our most valuable customers, tackling challenging problems, have a hand in shaping the future of cloud adoption, enhancing and growing your own skills, and having fun, then we would love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

You will be a critical partner to our customers, leveraging your experience with large scale cloud transformations and helping shepherd them through their stages of AWS adoption. Guiding the customer through the operational, educational, and governance aspects of a successful AWS cloud journey.

You will interface with customer and AWS leadership, driving collaboration between the other core account groups (Sales, Support, Solutions Architecture, and Professional Services), product/engineering teams, and customer teams, planning and supporting major workload migrations. You will translate strategic initiatives in the account plan into executable actions, working backwards from our customers key milestones. You will manage cadence by leading the reporting and tracking functions along the way. The execution of education plans, roadmap to business outcome alignments, Executive Briefing Sessions, and go-live events and transitions are a few items owned by the CSM that are critical to the success of our customer’s cloud journey.

You are encouraged to think big, invent and take ownership on customer challenges. You will not only bring the best of AWS/Amazon to our customers, you will proactively help solve the customer’s challenges through new ideas, tools and mechanisms.

Successful candidates will have a strong technical background, be aware of details that matter, have excellent problem-solving abilities, and be exemplary communicators both at the executive and project team level. You will be a peer leader, have the ability to gain stakeholder buy-in, negotiate and lead virtual teams. Your enterprise cloud experience and operational excellence will influence the team’s decisions, provide insight, and help drive secure and robust solutions.

You will evangelize AWS services and influence customers for adopting them. You should be passionate about delivering a great customer experience by deploying AWS solutions and driving innovation, and also be obsessed with contributing to the day-to-day management of customers’ successful migration to AWS.

Key job responsibilities

Responsibilities

You will establish a deep understanding of your customer’s business vision, culture and processes, and evangelize AWS services and influence customers to adopt the right solution at the right time. Customer Solution Managers (CSM) are responsible for four focus areas:

1/Accelerating AWS Adoption through Delivery and Execution

2/Identify & Align on Strategic Opportunities: CSMs work with the Customer Account team to work backwards from the customer to identify and pursue strategic cloud opportunities. These strategic cloud opportunities can include but are not limited to large-scale migrations, GenAI, data and analytics, digital innovation, high performance computing, product innovation, and business agility.

3/Customer Enablement, you will serve as the customer’s cloud journey coach and be the voice of the customer within AWS, evangelizing customer needs to AWS leadership, product, and engineering teams.

4/Implement governance structures to effectively govern both our partnership with the customer, and the customer’s adoption of AWS.

These interconnected focus areas will enable CSMs to effectively drive cloud adoption, pursue strategic growth opportunities, and empower customer success - all of which are critical to achieving the Automotive & Manufacturing IBU’s objectives. By aligning CSM activities, goals, and opportunities under these focus areas, the Automotive & Manufacturing CSM team can ensure a disciplined, customer-centric approach that maximizes business impact and revenue realization for AWS.

CSMs play a critical role supporting account teams/customers throughout the sales process, and the customer's cloud transformation journey, whilst consistently demonstrating measurable value to the customer regardless of engagement model.

CSMs are able to effectively coordinate cross-functional resources, drive disciplined project delivery, and quantify the tangible business benefits that customers realize through their cloud transformation initiatives. This holistic approach to customer engagement, coupled with the CSM's deep understanding of the Automotive & Manufacturing Industry and AWS capabilities; positions CSMs as trusted advisors who can guide customers through every stage of their cloud journey - from initial strategy and planning to migration, modernization, and ongoing optimization.

This position requires 15% - 30% travel across the calendar year to the customer.

Exceptional ability to lead through influence across diverse stakeholder groups

Critical thinking and self-motivation with proven ability to navigate ambiguity

Data-driven decision maker who uses metrics to measure success and drive improvements

Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with ability to tailor messaging to different audiences

Innovative mindset with passion for solving complex customer challenges

Potential for future career growth within the organization based on performance and alignment.

Description
The Center for Computational Biology (CCB), an in-house research center of the Simons Foundation ’s Flatiron Institute , is actively seeking enthusiastic, full-time post-doctoral Flatiron Research Fellows to join its Biological Transport & Networks Group .   The start date is flexible, with the Fellow expected to begin no later than September 2027. Applications will be reviewed beginning in Fall 2026 and considered on a rolling basis until the positions are filled.

ABOUT THE CENTER FOR COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY 

CCB has a twofold mission: to develop the rigorous modeling tools and theory needed for understanding biological processes, and to create computational frameworks that will facilitate the analysis of the large, complex data sets being generated by quantitative experimental technologies. To accomplish this, CCB brings together experts in various biological domains (including genomics, molecular, cellular, and developmental biology) whose approaches are informed by the modern computational tools of applied mathematics, statistical inference, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), biophysics, and computer science. The goal: to enable CCB to undertake ambitious, long-term research projects that transcend conventional disciplinary boundaries and that lead to a quantitative and predictive understanding of biological phenomena; and to develop high-quality, well-tested, versatile and extensible software across its research areas.  

CCB currently comprises more than 50 scientists at career stages from Ph.Ds through senior scientists, as well as visiting scientists and guest researchers, affiliated graduate students and interns. Together, the CCB scientific staff are pioneering an approach to biology in which theory,computation, and experimentation are integrated, from problem conceptualization onwards. This approach enables CCB to tackle not only recognized, fundamental problems in biology that have so far eluded solution, but also, because of the value placed on curiosity-driven research, to find and develop new areas of biological inquiry.

ABOUT THE BIOLOGICAL TRANSPORT & NETWORKS GROUP

Led by Eleni Katifori, the Biological Transport Networks group uses theory and computation, in close collaboration with experimentalists, to understand how biological networks develop, remodel, and function. We investigate how local physical processes—including fluid flow, tissue deformation, and transport of nutrients and signaling molecules—give rise to network architecture and collective behavior. Our work connects physics, applied mathematics, and biology, seeking general principles that explain both the diversity of transport networks across organisms and the common constraints that shape their organization.

Current research spans vertebrate vascular development and remodeling, circulation driven by cilia and body contractions in jellyfish, the interplay between tissue mechanics and vascular transport, and transport-informed models of neuronal growth and maturation. Central questions include how adaptation produces hierarchical or looped architectures, how pulsatile flows influence network development and function, and how nonlinearities and vessel compliance affect transport. We combine analytical models, large-scale numerical simulations, artificial intelligence and machine learning methods, and quantitative analysis of experimental data to connect processes at the scale of individual vessels with the behavior of entire networks. Alongside these biological questions, we investigate how adaptive physical networks can learn, store memory, and perform tasks through local interactions, with applications to fluidic and mechanical systems.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

Flatiron Research Fellows in CCB are individuals at the postdoctoral level with backgrounds in one or more of the following areas: applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines.

Reporting to the Group Lead, Fellows are expected to carry out an active research program that can be independently directed and/or involve substantial collaboration with other members of CCB or the Flatiron Institute. In addition to their research, Fellows help build the rich scientific community at CCB and the Flatiron Institute by participating in seminars, colloquia, and group meetings; developing their software, mathematical and computational expertise through internal education opportunities; and sharing their knowledge through scientific publications, presentations, and/or software releases, with the financial support of the Institute. Fellows have access to the Flatiron Institute’s powerful scientific computing resources.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Performing theoretical and computational research

Developing, implementing and maintaining scientific software

Participating in the organization of CCB and Flatiron-wide collaborative activities including seminars, workshops and meetings

Participating in the preparation of manuscripts for publication and of presentations at scientific conferences

Assisting in student mentorship

Sharing expertise and providing training and guidance to CCB staff and visitors as needed.

Fellows will be based, and have a principal office or workspace, at the Simons Foundation’s offices in New York City.  The initial appointments for Flatiron Research Fellows are generally for two years, with the possibility of renewal for a third year, contingent on performance. FRFs may be eligible for subsidized housing within walking distance of CCB. 
Qualifications
Education

Ph.D. in a relevant field (applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines)

Related Skills & Other Requirements

Demonstrated abilities in mathematical modeling, analysis and/or scientific computation, scientific software and algorithm development, data analysis and inference, and image analysis

Ability to do original and outstanding research in computational biology, and expertise in computational methods, data analysis, software and algorithm development, modeling machine learning, and scientific simulation 

Ability to work well in an interdisciplinary environment, and to collaborate with experimentalists

Strong oral and written communication, data documentation, and presentation skills

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The full-time annual compensation for this position is USD $95,000. In addition to competitive salaries, the Simons Foundation provides employees with an outstanding benefits package.

To apply, please submit the following via the application portal:

Cover Letter, which should include a summary of applicants’ most significant contributions in graduate school

Curriculum vitae with publications list and, if relevant, links to software 

Research statement of no more than three (3) pages describing the applicant’s past important results, current and future research interests which may include both scientific topics and algorithm and software development, and potential synergies with activities at CCB

Two (2) letters of recommendation 

Applications will generally be reviewed beginning November 2026, and will be considered on a rolling basis until the positions are filled. For full consideration, candidates are strongly encouraged to submit their complete application by November 30, 2026. 

SELECTION CRITERIA

Applications will be evaluated based on: 

past research accomplishments

the proposed research program

the synergy of applicant’s expertise and research proposal topic with existing CCB staff and research programs, and potential to cross boundaries between CCB groups and/or the Flatiron Institute’s other research centers.

Any queries about the application process or about CCB should be directed to ccbjobs@flatironinstitute.org. Queries about CCB may also be directed to scientific staff at CCB.

The Flatiron Institute values authenticity, originality, and transparency throughout the application and hiring process. Applicants are expected to submit application materials that reflect their own original work, experiences, ideas, writing, and scientific or professional judgment. The use of AI-based tools may be appropriate for limited purposes during the hiring process, such as editing, formatting, or code review. The execution of education plans, roadmap to business outcome alignments, Executive Briefing Sessions, and go-live events and transitions are a few items owned by the CSM that are critical to the success of our customer’s cloud journey.

Exceptional ability to lead through influence across diverse stakeholder groups

Critical thinking and self-motivation with proven ability to navigate ambiguity

Data-driven decision maker who uses metrics to measure success and drive improvements

We are excited to offer a Fall 2026 internship opportunity designed for college students in the La Jolla, San Diego area who are able to commute to our office. Run recurring data-extraction jobs, such as pulling figures from HOA financial-statement PDFs into structured spreadsheets.
Support data cleanup, entry, and validation in our Supabase platform and across spreadsheets.
Help design, build, and test internal tools and dashboards that staff use day to day: including early versions of tools that could replace software we currently buy.
Maintain data quality in HubSpot, and support the competitive-intelligence and acquisition research process by gathering, organizing, scoring, and verifying company and contact data.
Document how workflows and tools function, and take ownership of well-defined projects from start to finish.

Outside-the-box thinking. You don’t just complete the task in front of you. Ask whether there’s a smarter way to do it, and you’re eager to test your ideas rather than wait for permission.
Self-direction. Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work independently in an unstructured, fast-paced environment with minimal hands-on oversight.

Analytical aptitude. Strong analytical skills and an aptitude for breaking down data and business problems.
Communication. Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with diverse team members and explain what you built and why.
Genuine interest. Real curiosity for technology, automation, and AI, and how they can transform how a business operates.
Benefits
Gain hands-on experience with a real production stack – automation (n8n), databases (Supabase/Postgres), CRMs (HubSpot), and applied AI – skills that transfer to almost any modern company.
Work on genuinely ambitious problems, not busywork, with room to propose and test your own ideas.
Work closely with experienced professionals in a collaborative, mentorship-oriented environment.
Access valuable networking opportunities within the technology and business community.
Flexible work arrangements to accommodate academic commitments.
Real projects you can point to, plus exposure to many aspects of how a growing business runs on technology.
Potential for future career growth within the organization based on performance and alignment.

Job Title: R&D Technician

Job Description

The R&D Technician supports product development by assembling and configuring prototype equipment and systems, building custom test fixtures, and maintaining a specialized R&D test facility for HVAC and industrial equipment. This role combines hands-on mechanical and electrical work with troubleshooting, calibration, and general facility upkeep to ensure accurate testing, reliable equipment performance, and a safe, well-organized lab environment.

Responsibilities

Assemble and configure prototype equipment and systems to support product development initiatives.
Build and install custom test fixtures, rigs, and setups to enable validation and performance testing of products.
Maintain, calibrate, and upgrade test labs and equipment to ensure accuracy, reliability, and compliance with relevant standards.
Diagnose and resolve issues with equipment, products, and testing facilities, including mechanical, electrical, and control-related problems.
Perform routine preventative maintenance on mechanical, electrical, and testing equipment to minimize downtime and extend asset life.
Carry out general building maintenance tasks as needed, including minor repairs and upkeep of workspaces and equipment areas.
Use precision measuring tools and test equipment to verify performance and ensure proper operation of prototypes and test rigs.
Read and interpret mechanical drawings, blueprints, electrical schematics, and technical manuals to guide assembly and troubleshooting.
Apply safe and effective practices when working with mains voltage, low voltage systems, and high voltage circuits.
Troubleshoot PLC-controlled systems and test equipment as needed to support R&D testing and automation.
Manage multiple concurrent tasks and projects efficiently while maintaining strong attention to detail and meeting deadlines.
Document work performed, including maintenance activities, test setups, and configuration changes, in a clear and organized manner.
Collaborate effectively with engineers and other team members, providing feedback and suggestions to improve products, processes, and test setups.

Essential Skills

High School Diploma or GED equivalent.
Hands-on experience assembling equipment, industrial products, and machinery in a development or R&D setting, with at least 3+ years of experience in assembly of equipment or industrial products.
Proficiency in mechanical assembly, including alignment, fastening, and integration of components.
Skilled in electrical assembly, wiring, and cable routing for industrial and prototype systems.
Solid understanding of basic electrical principles, including mains voltage, low voltage, and high voltage systems.
Ability to read and interpret blueprints, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, and technical manuals.
Competence in the safe and effective use of hand tools, power tools, precision instruments, and electrical testing equipment.
Experience with troubleshooting mechanical, electrical, and industrial machinery issues in an R&D or test environment.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to build strong working relationships across teams.
Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail and a proactive approach to problem solving.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while managing multiple projects simultaneously.
Ability to lift up to 40 lbs occasionally.

Work Environment

The role is based in an R&D test facility

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Orange, CA.

Job Summary And Responsibilities

As our Clinical Lab Scientist, you will be a critical diagnostic expert, performing complex laboratory tests to ensure accurate, timely results vital for patient diagnosis and treatment.

Every day, you will execute a wide range of analytical procedures across various lab disciplines (hematology, chemistry, microbiology, etc.). You'll analyze specimens, operate/maintain instruments, interpret results, and conduct quality control, providing crucial data for clinical decisions.

To be successful in this role, you must demonstrate a strong scientific foundation, advanced technical proficiency, exceptional problem-solving skills, and meticulous attention to detail. Your paramount commitment will be to accuracy and regulatory adherence.

Interacts with physician, nurses, ward clerks, phlebotomists, other clinical laboratory scientists and other health care professionals in the resolution of problems involving patient specimen collection and handling, appropriateness of specimens, clarification of orders and result reporting.
Consults with Clinical Laboratory Scientists, Laboratory Supervisors, Administrative Director of Laboratory Services, Medical Director of Laboratory Services, or Pathologists for policy clarification and problem resolution.
Operates lab computer system according to manuals in each department.
Familiarity and compliance with general laboratory safety practices, MSDS guidelines, State of California regulations and requirements, OSHA standards, CDC recommendation and universal precautions.
Participates in the clinical laboratory scientist teaching program to assist in the training of Clinical Laboratory Scientist students, MLT students, or other established programs.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Job Requirements

Minimum Requirements:

CA Clinical Lab Scientist
Must have the ability to speak, read and write English

Preferred Skills

One year acute care hospital experience preferred
Above average communication and organizational skills
Ability to adapt to workload demands and function efficiently during difficult or emergency situations
Ability to maintain and operate laboratory equipment
Familiarity with medical terminology, basic computer terminology and data entry skills
Ability to follow written and verbal instructions
American Society Clinical Path (CT ASCP)

Where You'll Work

Founded in 1910, Dignity Health - Mercy Hospital is a 229-bed, acute care, nonprofit hospital located in Bakersfield, California. Serving nearly 90,000 patients annually, the hospital offers a full complement of services including Level II NICU, cancer care, women’s health, and orthopedics. Additionally, Mercy Hospital Downtown & Mercy Hospital Southwest have been recognized as an LGBTQ+ Healthcare Equality High Performer by the Human Rights Campaign Foundation. They are both Joint Commission-certified Primary Stroke Centers. Mercy Hospital Downtown offers the only inpatient Oncology Unit in Bakersfield while Mercy Hospital Southwest has the only Obstetric Emergency Department in Bakersfield.
